title: Strategy Executability in Mathematical Reasoning: Leveraging Human-Model Differences for Effective Guidance
abstract: arXiv:2602.22583v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Example-based guidance is widely used to improve mathematical reasoning at inference time, yet its effectiveness is highly unstable across problems and models-even when the guidance is correct and problem-relevant. We show that this instability arises from a previously underexplored gap between strategy usage-whether a reasoning strategy appears in successful solutions-and strategy executability-whether the strategy remains effective when instantiated as guidance for a target model. Through a controlled analysis of paired human-written and model-generated solutions, we identify a systematic dissociation between usage and executability: human- and model-derived strategies differ in structured, domain-dependent ways, leading to complementary strengths and consistent source-dependent reversals under guidance. translated_title: 数学推理中的策略可执行性：利用人类与模型的差异实现有效引导
translated_abstract: 基于示例的引导被广泛用于在推理阶段提升数学推理能力，然而其效果在不同问题与模型之间极不稳定——即使引导本身是正确且与问题相关的。我们证明这种不稳定性源于一个此前未被充分探索的差距，即“策略使用”（某种推理策略是否出现在成功的解答中）与“策略可执行性”（当该策略被实例化为针对目标模型的引导时是否依然有效）之间的差距。通过对成对的人类撰写解答与模型生成解答进行受控分析，我们识别出使用与可执行性之间的系统性分离：人类推导的策略与模型推导的策略在结构化、领域依赖的方式上存在差异，从而形成了互补的优势，并在引导下产生一致的、依赖于策略来源的反转现象。基于这一诊断，我们提出了选择性策略检索，这是一个在测试时显式建模策略可执行性的框架。
tldr: 该论文揭示了数学推理中“策略使用”与“策略可执行性”之间的系统性差距，并提出选择性策略检索（SSR）测试时框架，通过显式建模可执行性并利用人类策略与模型策略的互补差异来实现更有效的推理引导。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals a systematic gap between strategy usage and strategy executability in mathematical reasoning, and proposes Selective Strategy Retrieval (SSR), a test-time framework that explicitly models executability and leverages the complementary differences between human- and model-derived strategies for more effective guidance.
